recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-25397 unless future Patient Care work changes the semantics of AdverseEvent.encounter.
issue_request: FHIR-25397 requested that AdverseEvent.encounter be clarified so the short description and definition identify the Encounter associated with the start of the AdverseEvent, and the comments explain that the associated encounter is where the triggering activity occurred rather than a later reporting encounter.
initial_application: The Jira comment points to commit faf138c4d650f25e2afb3d1d86f7a8dfac2cd07b, which applied the requested wording to the then-authoritative AdverseEvent spreadsheet source. Later source refactoring in 33b409a4b6 moved the resource to structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml while preserving the text, and 086649a235 added the Event mapping exception file with the same AdverseEvent-specific wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes AdverseEvent in the current build, and both the current StructureDefinition and Event mapping exception source contain the requested short, definition, and comments. Patient Care minutes from 2019-12-19 reference FHIR-25397 and the goal of aligning encounter comments with the definition. A Zulip search for the issue terms found no conflicting community discussion. FHIR-25396 was co-applied in the same historical commit but concerns AdverseEvent.category, not AdverseEvent.encounter.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source edit was needed because the current build-scope source already implements the issue decision.

related_jiras.note: Co-applied in the same historical commit, but it concerns the AdverseEvent category value set rather than the encounter element and was not decided here.
